hints.title: Value Ranking and Index Retention
hints.text: Pair each array value with its original index before sorting by magnitude.

hints.title: Top K Selection
hints.text: Extract the k elements with the greatest values.

hints.title: Index Order Restoration
hints.text: Sort the chosen k elements by their original indices and project back to values.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def maxSubsequence(self, nums: list[int], k: int) -> list[int]:
        indexed = [(val, idx) for idx, val in enumerate(nums)]
        top_k = sorted(indexed, key=lambda x: x[0], reverse=True)[:k]
        top_k.sort(key=lambda x: x[1])
        return [val for val, idx in top_k]
```

complexity.time: O(N log N) sorting values and restoring original index ordering
complexity.notes: Select the k largest elements while maintaining their original relative order in the array.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing every subsequence of size k takes exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Storing indices alongside values allows re-sorting by original index.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should preserve original relative index ordering after identifying the top k values.
